skills.name: benchmarking
skills.description: Guide for building, running, and analyzing Nanvix performance benchmarks. Use this when asked about benchmark setup, execution, or interpretation.

skills.name: build
skills.description: Guide for building, formatting, linting, and spell-checking Nanvix with z. Use this when asked to build or validate the repository.

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline
skills.description: Guide for Nanvix CI and GitHub Actions workflow behavior, including local pipeline execution and matrix coverage. Use this when asked about CI checks, workflow failures, or release flow.

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development
skills.description: Guide for developing and debugging Nanvix daemons, including guest daemons and host linuxd behavior. Use this when asked about daemon architecture or daemon changes.

skills.name: gdb-debugging
skills.description: Guide for debugging Nanvix guests using GDB remote debugging over the microvm machine type. Use this when asked about attaching GDB, setting breakpoints, or stepping through kernel code.

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development
skills.description: Guide for creating and modifying Nanvix libraries under src/libs, including guest no_std and host std crates. Use this when asked about library architecture or crate changes.

skills.name: test-development
skills.description: Guide for writing, running, and debugging Nanvix unit, integration, and system tests in Rust and C/C++. Use this when asked about test implementation or failures.

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: troubleshooting
skills.description: Guide for diagnosing Nanvix build, runtime, and test failures, including cleanup and debugging workflows. Use this when asked to investigate errors or unstable behavior.

skills.name: user-app-development
skills.description: Guide for developing, building, and running Nanvix user-space applications across supported runtimes and languages. Use this when asked about guest app implementation or execution.

skills.name: find-skills
skills.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

skills.name: customize-cloud-agent
skills.description: Skill for customizing the Copilot cloud agent (formerly known as Copilot coding agent) environment, including copilot-setup-steps.yml configuration, preinstalling tools and dependencies, runners, and settings. Use when the user mentions copilot-setup-steps, copilot setup steps, or wants to configure the cloud agent environment.

1. verus! {
2. 
3. impl KernelFrame {
4.     /// Well-formedness of a kernel-frame handle: its owned physical address is page aligned.
5.     ///
6.     /// Purely structural — it makes **no** ownership claim (it does not assert that the frame
7.     /// is allocated). Page alignment is the one caller-visible fact `base()`'s consumers rely on:
8.     /// `into_page_address` and the `KernelStack` index arithmetic behind it assume the returned
9.     /// `FrameAddress` is page aligned. Stated entirely on the abstract address `self@`, so it
10.     /// leaks no implementation detail. Mirror of `UserFrame::inv`.
11.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
12.         self@ % crate::hal::mem::spec_page_size() == 0
13.     }
14. }
15. 
16. } // verus!
17.

1. // Copyright(c) The Maintainers of Nanvix.
2. // Licensed under the MIT License.
3. 
4. //! Kernel frame type.
5. //!
6. //! A [`KernelFrame`] represents a single page-sized physical frame allocated for kernel use.
7. //! It provides `Deref`/`DerefMut` for direct kernel access (identity-mapped) and frees the
8. //! underlying frame on drop via the global frame allocator.
9. 
10. //==================================================================================================
11. // Imports
12. //==================================================================================================
13. 
14. use vstd::prelude::*;
15. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
16. include!("kframe.spec.rs");
17. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
18. include!("kframe.proof.rs");
19. 
20. use crate::hal::mem::{
21.     Address,
22.     FrameAddress,
23.     PageAligned,
24.     PhysicalAddress,
25. };
26. use ::arch::mem;
27. use ::core::ops::{
28.     Deref,
29.     DerefMut,
30. };
31. use ::sys::error::Error;
32. 
33. //==================================================================================================
34. // Kernel Frame
35. //==================================================================================================
36. 
37. /// A type that represents a kernel frame.
38. #[derive(Debug)]
39. #[verus_verify(external_derive)]
40. pub struct KernelFrame {
41.     /// Frame address.
42.     base: FrameAddress,
43. }
44. 
45. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
46. verus! {
47. 
48. /// Abstract view of a kernel frame: the physical address of the owned frame.
49. impl View for KernelFrame {
50.     type V = int;
51. 
52.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> int {
53.         self.base@
54.     }
55. }
56. 
57. } // verus!
58. 
59. // Dependency contract for the manager layer: wrapping a `FrameAddress` produces a handle whose
60. // abstract address is the same physical frame.
61. #[verus_verify]
62. impl KernelFrame {
63.     ///
64.     /// # Description
65.     ///
66.     /// Instantiates a kernel frame.
67.     ///
68.     /// # Parameters
69.     ///
70.     /// - `base`: Frame address.
71.     ///
72.     /// # Returns
73.     ///
74.     /// Upon success, a kernel frame is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
75.     ///
76.     // Dependency contract: wrapping a frame goes through `mm::virt::identity_map_page`, which
77.     // is outside the verification scope of `mm::phys`. On success the returned handle owns the
78.     // same physical frame that was passed in. `external_body` per `verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md`:
79.     // the identity-mapping side effect lives in `mm::virt` and the body's `?`/log closures call
80.     // into that layer, so the wrap contract is trusted until `mm::virt` is verified.
81.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
82.     #[verus_spec(result =>
83.         requires
84.             base.inv(),
85.         ensures
86.             match result {
87.                 Ok(kf) => {
88.                     &&& kf@ == base@
89.                     &&& kf.inv()
90.                 },
91.                 Err(_) => true,
92.             },
93.     )]
94.     pub(super) fn new(base: FrameAddress) -> Result<Self, Error> {
95.         // Ensure the frame is identity-mapped in the kernel address space so that
96.         // Deref/DerefMut can safely access it. This lazily installs a page
97.         // table entry if needed (page tables come from a BSS pool, so no recursive frame
98.         // allocation occurs).
99.         let phys_addr: PageAligned<PhysicalAddress> =
100.             PageAligned::from_raw_value(base.into_raw_value()).map_err(|e| {
101.                 error!("frame base is not page-aligned: {e:?}");
102.                 e
103.             })?;
104.         crate::mm::virt::identity_map_page(phys_addr).map_err(|e| {
105.             error!("failed to identity-map frame: {:?}", e);
106.             e
107.         })?;
108. 
109.         Ok(Self { base })
110.     }
111. }
112. 
113. #[verus_verify]
114. impl KernelFrame {
115. 
116.     ///
117.     /// # Description
118.     ///
119.     /// Returns the base address of the target kernel frame.
120.     ///
121.     /// # Returns
122.     ///
123.     /// The base address of the target kernel frame.
124.     ///
125.     // Pure accessor: returns the owned frame's physical address unchanged. `result@ == self@`
126.     // gives `kpage` the exact address; `result.inv()` (page alignment carried from `self.inv()`)
127.     // lets `into_page_address` and the `KernelStack` arithmetic behind it proceed.
128.     #[verus_spec(result =>
129.         requires
130.             self.inv(),
131.         ensures
132.             result@ == self@,
133.             result.inv(),
134.     )]
135.     pub fn base(&self) -> FrameAddress {
136.         self.base
137.     }
138. }
139. 
140. impl KernelFrame {
141. 
142.     ///
143.     /// # Description
144.     ///
145.     /// Clears the target kernel frame.
146.     ///
147.     /// Uses the identity-map `memset` backend so that the write runs in the kernel address space.
148.     /// This avoids a page fault when the current CR3 points to a user page directory that lacks
149.     /// the PDE for this frame's physical address.
150.     ///
151.     pub fn clear(&mut self) -> Result<(), Error> {
152.         let base: *mut u8 = self.base.into_raw_value() as *mut u8;
153.         crate::mm::virt::memset(base, 0, mem::PAGE_SIZE).map_err(|e| {
154.             error!("memset failed: {:?}", e);
155.             e
156.         })
157.     }
158. }
159. 
160. /// # Safety
161. ///
162. /// `Deref` accesses the identity-mapped frame directly. The caller must ensure that the current
163. /// CR3 points to a page directory that has the relevant PDE for this frame's physical address
164. /// (i.e., the kernel page directory, or a user page directory into which the PDE has been
165. /// propagated via [`sync_kernel_pdes`](crate::mm::virt::sync_kernel_pdes)). For CR3-agnostic
166. /// writes, prefer [`KernelFrame::clear()`] which uses the identity-map `memset` backend.
167. impl Deref for KernelFrame {
168.     type Target = [u8];
169. 
170.     fn deref(&self) -> &Self::Target {
171.         let ptr: usize = self.base.into_raw_value();
172.         unsafe { core::slice::from_raw_parts(ptr as *const u8, mem::PAGE_SIZE) }
173.     }
174. }
175. 
176. /// # Safety
177. ///
178. /// See [`Deref`] impl — the same CR3 invariant applies.
179. impl DerefMut for KernelFrame {
180.     fn deref_mut(&mut self) -> &mut Self::Target {
181.         let ptr: usize = self.base.into_raw_value();
182.         unsafe { core::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(ptr as *mut u8, mem::PAGE_SIZE) }
183.     }
184. }
185. 
186. #[verus_verify]
187. impl Drop for KernelFrame {
188.     // Releasing the handle returns its physical frame to the global frame allocator via
189.     // `super::frame::free`, which is best-effort (`ensures true`) and `opens_invariants none`/
190.     // `no_unwind`, so `drop` makes no abstract postcondition. Callers (the manager error path,
191.     // `KernelStack::drop`) rely on this being the sole, complete deallocation step. Mirror of
192.     // `UserFrame::drop`.
193.     #[verus_spec(
194.         opens_invariants none
195.         no_unwind
196.     )]
197.     fn drop(&mut self) {
198.         if let Err(e) = super::frame::free(self.base) {
199.             #[cfg(not(verus_keep_ghost))]
200.             error!("failed to free kernel frame: {:?}", e);
201.         }
202.     }
203. }

 Large inline proof blocks hurt readability and make exec code hard to review.

    - `ensures`: the property being proven (must be strong enough for the call site)
 3. Replace the inline block with a 1-3 line lemma call.

 Lemma names describe what they prove:
 - ✅ `lemma_set_bit_preserves_inv`
 - ✅ `lemma_alloc_range_bounded`
 - ❌ `lemma_proof_block_1`
 - ❌ `lemma_helper`

 - Do NOT change exec logic.
 - Do NOT change spec function signatures.

result.content:
1. ---
2. name: proof-minimization
3. description: "Remove redundant proof artifacts (assertions, lemmas, hints, dead code) without weakening guarantees. Use when polishing verified code to reduce verbosity."
4. ---
5. 
6. # Proof Minimization
7. 
8. Remove redundant proof artifacts to make verification lean and readable
9. without weakening any guarantees.
10. 
11. ## What to Remove
12. 
13. 1. **Redundant lemmas** — another lemma proves the exact same property
14.    (same `requires` AND same `ensures`).
15. 2. **Redundant assertions** — `assert` statements that Verus can verify
16.    without them. Remove in bulk, then re-run verification.
17. 3. **Redundant proof hints** — unnecessary `by`, `by(nonlinear_arith)`,
18.    or trigger annotations that Verus doesn't need.
19. 4. **Dead spec functions** — non-public spec functions with zero callers (not
20.    referenced in any `requires`, `ensures`, `invariant`, or lemma). Keep
21.    `pub` spec functions — they may be part of the module's API for dependents.
22. 5. **Debug artifacts** — In spec/proof files: remove TODO comments, commented-out
23.    code, and property-ID annotations (e.g., `// FUNC-POST-3`, `// INV-2`). In
24.    exec files: remove unnecessary verification-related comments (e.g., obsolete
25.    proof hints, property-ID tags); do NOT remove original source comments.
26. 
27. ## What is NOT Redundant
28. 
29. - **Uncalled lemmas**: Verus verifies all lemmas regardless of callers.
30.   An uncalled lemma still proves a property. Only remove if another lemma
31.   proves the *exact* same thing.
32. - **Different preconditions**: Two lemmas with different `requires` prove
33.   different properties even if `ensures` looks similar.
34. 
35. **When in doubt, keep it.**
36. 
37. ## Process
38. 
39. This is a best-effort pass for readability, not an exhaustive search.
40. 
41. 1. **Assertions**: Remove `assert` statements that look redundant based on context.
42. 2. **Lemmas**: Remove a lemma only if another has identical `requires` + `ensures`.
43. 3. **Proof hints**: Remove `by(...)` annotations that look unnecessary.
44. 4. Re-run verification after changes — if it fails, revert the removal.
45. 
46. ## Constraints
47. 
48. - Do NOT add `assume`, `admit`, or `external_body`.
49. - Do NOT weaken any `ensures` or remove any meaningful property.
50. - Verification must pass after every removal batch.
51.
